instrument_review:

instrument_review:
DesignQA review using the original EFPA Test Review Model 2025, version 5.0. Perspective: familiar with AI use but new to benchmarks; this is a simulated review, not an expert certification. The supplied passages support inspection of AI performance on specified Formula SAE tasks. Documented scoring sensitivities, unequal information supply and limited reproducibility constrain comparisons. All numbered descriptive fields and evaluative items are addressed below, sometimes grouped explicitly. No aggregate quality score is calculated.

Reviewed version: the original benchmark in the 2024 paper and public scoring software. Sources were inspected on 6 October 2026; that is not the date of this simulated review.

supported_claims[7]:

Six task groups ask AI systems to retrieve and apply rules or interpret terminology and visual materials. Answers receive group-specific scores, and software reports an equally weighted group composite. Evaluated systems can differ in their information supply. No human-engineer baseline or score norms are reported.

documented_problems[0]:
6.1.3.3; 10.1: One rulebook and a limited task range constrain content coverage. Group sizes range from 1,192 individual-rule questions to 16 performance questions.

documented_problems[1]:
3.2; 6.3.2: Wording and formatting can change credit. Documented examples include missing commas and valid related rules omitted from supplied answers.

documented_problems[2]:
3.2; 10.2: The overall score weights groups equally despite unequal sizes and different marking methods. The packet does not establish a distinct skill interpretation for this composite or its components; equal weighting alone is not proof of invalidity.

documented_problems[3]:
2.8; 11.5=1: Systems receive different information supplies. This demonstrably confounds comparisons interpreted as differences between the AI models alone; results describe models together with their supplied information.

documented_problems[4]:
9.7: The five passage-set evaluations change the supplied evidence, so they do not isolate identical-condition repeatability. In the 16-question performance group, one additional correct answer changes accuracy by the stated 6.25 percentage points.

documented_problems[5]:
6.1.7=1: All described scale-bar drawings comply with the rule, permitting an always-yes answer to obtain binary credit on that portion. This is a documented item-balance weakness for discriminating compliance judgement; it does not show that any tested AI used the shortcut, and it does not cover explanation credit.

documented_problems[6]:
6.3.8=1: Historical software, settings and inputs are not fully linked to every published result, preventing complete replication from the inspected materials.

documented_problems[7]:
7.1.7: A released answer file has fewer rows than the corresponding paper count. The scope and effect of that mismatch are not established.

documented_problems[8]:
11.8=1: Support for unqualified model-only comparison is inadequate because information supply differs and precise comparative uncertainty is unresolved. Comparisons restricted to explicitly identified model-plus-input configurations remain more defensible.

documented_problems[9]:
10.5: The paper itself leaves performance on other technical documents uncertain. Authentic vehicle materials do not demonstrate predictive validity for other standards or real engineering projects.

instrument_review:
Condition-native review of ARC-AGI-2 public problems, inspected official scoring software and ARC Prize verified-testing rules. The supplied passages support interpretation as performance on unfamiliar grid tasks under specified conditions. Broader reasoning interpretations and the precision of AI comparisons remain unresolved. All numbered EFPA descriptive fields and evaluative items are addressed below; grouped IDs share the stated rationale. No aggregate quality score is calculated.

instrument_review:
Condition-native review of the original 2024 DesignQA benchmark and supplied account of public scoring software. Scores describe performance on the sampled Formula SAE tasks with the tested information-supply arrangements. Broader engineering competence, latent skill interpretations and fine rankings are not established. All numbered EFPA descriptive fields and evaluative items are addressed below; grouped IDs share the stated rationale. No aggregate quality score is calculated.
